question: Wasim travels 455 km at 91 km/hr, the next 390 km at 78 km/hr and the next 476 km at 68 km/hr. What is his average speed (in km/hr) for the whole journey? (Round off your answer to two decimal places)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Time = (455 ÷ 91) + (390 ÷ 78) + (476 ÷ 68) = 5 + 5 + 7 = 17 hr

Total Distance = 455 + 390 + 476 = 1321 km

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ Average Speed = 1321 ÷ 17 ≈ 77.71 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 77.71 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

D₂ = 390 km, S₂ = 78 km/hr

D₃ = 476 km, S₃ = 68 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Distance)

When two equal distances are covered at speeds x and y, the average speed is 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Average Speed (Equal Time)

When travelling at speeds x and y for equal amounts of time, the average speed is (x + y) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed

When two bodies move in the same direction, relative speed is |x − y|. In opposite directions, it is (x + y).
